correctness.rationale: For d>=3 every translated reflected simplex corresponds to a nonnegative cap vector of sum two; exact inclusion–exclusion computes overlap. Concavity of its d-th volume root and strict Brunn–Minkowski equality conditions force the optimum under a fixed excluded coordinate to have one exceptional cap and d equal caps. A distinct faceted intersection argument makes the two-level maximum strictly increasing until 2/(d+1). This yields the depth formula for every y, homothetic upper regions, exact contact height, complete Dirichlet survival law and exact baseline atom. Independent exact rational subset formulas and sampled exclusion tests (68,437 checks) passed; finite checks are not the proof.

value.rationale: The orientation-reversed simplex problem produces an all-dimensional, fully explicit solution for geometric depth. It identifies both the shape and measure of its nontrivial regions, a sharp support-contact threshold, and a probability atom equal to the baseline depth. The d=3 profile and exponential degeneration of higher-dimensional mass provide natural nontrivial benchmarks for the new translate-depth framework. This is not merely the known maximum-spacing CDF or the earlier planar formula.
